shared_elements: circular/disc-like motif (incised disc on A, rosette-like curls on B)
horizontal band of repeated marks near the top (incised signs on A, inscription band on B)
parallel linear striations used as filler pattern
justification: Both are stone surfaces worked in relief with a band of small repeated signs across the upper zone and some use of a disc/roundel motif plus parallel incised striations, which is about as far as the correspondence goes. Otherwise they differ fundamentally: A is a weathered, upright, schematic monolith with shallow, abstracted engraved motifs and no recognisable figure, while B is a rectangular panel bearing a crisply modelled, anatomically detailed winged bird-headed figure in profile, carved in confident high relief.
